sub: Named after Muḥammad ﷺ in ayah 2; also called al-Qitāl, “fighting”, from ayah 20
theme: Two camps and their ends: disbelievers whose deeds are wasted, and believers whose affairs Allah sets right. It prepares the believers to fight, exposes the hypocrites, and calls for courage and spending.
story: Revealed in Madinah after the Hijrah, once fighting had been made a duty. The Muslims were few and poor, and surrounded by enemies set on wiping them out. Reports differ on timing: some place it before any battle, others link parts of it to Badr and Uḥud.

The surah prepares them. It sets out the two camps, gives orders for battle and captives, and promises help to those who support Allah. Ayah 13 reportedly came as the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah, the city he loved, driven out by its people.

When the order to fight came, the hypocrites panicked and secretly sided with the enemy. So the surah exposes them, tells the believers not to weaken or seek peace from weakness, and calls them to spend, warning that Allah can replace them.

sections.title: Disbelievers’ deeds wasted, believers’ sins erased: falsehood versus truth from their Lord
sections.meaning: Those who disbelieve and block others from Allah’s way have their deeds wasted. Those who believe, do good and believe in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ have their sins removed and their condition set right. The reason: one side follows falsehood, the other follows the truth from their Lord.
points: Disbelievers who block Allah’s way: their deeds are wasted
Believers in what came to Muḥammad ﷺ: sins removed, condition set right
Why: falsehood versus truth; so Allah sets out their examples
sections.matters: It opens with the surah’s two camps and its key word, aʿmāl (deeds). What follows, the fighting, the hypocrites and the spending, all turns on which camp a person is really in, and whether his deeds will count.
sections.story: No single agreed incident. The disbelievers are reportedly Makkah’s leaders, and one report names the men who fed the Quraysh army at Badr. The believers are reportedly the Anṣār. Others say both descriptions are general.
explained: Kafarū wa ṣaddū: they disbelieved and blocked others from Islam. Aḍalla aʿmālahum: Allah makes their deeds go to waste. That covers their plots against the Prophet ﷺ, which fail, and even their good deeds, like feeding guests and keeping family ties, because deeds need faith to count in the Hereafter.

The believers have their sins wiped away and their bāl set right: their condition, or their hearts, in this world and the next. Believing in what was sent to Muḥammad ﷺ is named on its own, because after his coming true faith means following him. The cause of both outcomes: falsehood versus truth.
teaches: Good deeds need faith to count.
Believing in the Prophet ﷺ and what he brought is part of true faith.
What you follow decides where your deeds end up.
Allah sets right the affairs of those who follow the truth.
sections.hook: The surah starts on page 507, and ayah 2 holds the name Muḥammad. Ayah 3 is a mirror: those who disbelieve follow al-bāṭil; those who believe follow al-ḥaqq.

sections.title: Rules for battle and captives; martyrs rewarded; support Allah, He supports you
sections.meaning: In battle, fight until the enemy is overwhelmed, then bind the captives and later free them, as a favour or for ransom. Allah could defeat them Himself, but He tests people through each other. Those killed in His cause never lose their deeds. Support Allah and He supports you; the disbelievers are ruined.
points: Fight, bind captives, free by favour or ransom; the slain lose nothing
He guides them, sets them right, admits them to a known Paradise
Support Allah: He supports you and makes your feet firm
Disbelievers ruined, deeds wasted, because they hated His revelation
sections.matters: It gives a small, threatened community its first battle instructions, and answers the fear behind them: Allah could win without you, the struggle is a test, and nothing given in His cause is lost.
sections.story: Reports differ. Ayah 4 reportedly came after Badr, where taking ransom for captives had been criticised, and now allowed release by favour or ransom. Its ending, about those killed, reportedly came at Uḥud, when many Muslims had been killed or wounded.
explained: Fa-ḍarba ar-riqāb, strike the necks: fight fully until you have overwhelmed them. Then bind the captives firmly so they can’t escape. Afterwards free them either as mann, a favour with nothing taken, or for fidāʾ, a ransom of money or an exchange for Muslim captives, until the war lays down its burdens. Jurists differed on whether this was later changed.

Allah could punish them without any fighting, but He tests people through one another to show who is true. Those killed in His cause never lose their deeds: He guides them, sets them right and brings them into a Paradise He made known to them. Support His religion and He makes your feet firm; the disbelievers get taʿs, ruin.
teaches: Allah could win without us; the struggle tests who is true.
Nothing done or given for Allah is ever lost.
Support Allah’s religion and He supports you and steadies your feet.
Hating what Allah revealed wipes out a person’s deeds.
sections.hook: Ayah 5 echoes ayah 2: aṣlaḥa bālahum → yuṣliḥu bālahum. Aʿmālahum ends ayat 1, 4, 8 and 9. Ayah 7 is the first of two “O you who have believed” calls; the other is 33.

sections.title: Past nations destroyed, Makkah warned; Paradise’s rivers versus scalding water for deniers
sections.meaning: Earlier deniers were destroyed; these face the same, because Allah protects the believers and the disbelievers have no protector. Believers enter gardens; disbelievers eat like cattle and end in the Fire. Towns stronger than Makkah fell. One on clear proof is not like one following desires, just as Paradise’s rivers are not like scalding water.
points: Look at earlier nations; Allah protects believers, disbelievers have none
Gardens for believers; disbelievers eat like cattle, the Fire their home
Towns stronger than Makkah, which drove you out, were destroyed
Clear proof from his Lord versus evil made to look good
Rivers of water, milk, wine and honey versus scalding water
sections.matters: It gives the believers, then few and weak, confidence: Allah is their mawlā and the enemy has none. It warns Makkah, which had driven the Prophet ﷺ out, and makes the two ends so vivid that no one could think the camps equal.
sections.story: Ayah 11 echoes Uḥud, where the Muslims answered the enemy’s boast: “Allah is our protector, and you have none.” Ayah 13 reportedly came as the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah, saying he would never have left had its people not driven him out.
explained: Have they not travelled and seen how earlier nations ended? Allah destroyed them, and Makkah’s disbelievers face the like. Allah is the mawlā, the protector, of the believers; the disbelievers have none. So believers enter gardens with flowing rivers, while disbelievers enjoy and eat like cattle, caring for nothing beyond this world, and the Fire is their home.

Many towns stronger than Makkah were destroyed with no one to help. Is one on clear proof from his Lord like one whose evil looks good to him? Paradise has rivers of fresh water, unchanging milk, delicious wine and pure honey, with every fruit and forgiveness. The other side drinks boiling water that tears their insides.
teaches: With Allah as your protector, numbers and strength don’t decide the outcome.
Living only to enjoy and eat is living like cattle.
Power did not save past nations, and it saves no one now.
Following desire makes evil look good.
Paradise’s blessings are pure, with none of this world’s flaws.
sections.hook: “No protector for them” (lā mawlā lahum, 11) is followed by “no helper for them” (13). Ayat 14 and 15 both ask “…like one who” (ka-man). Rivers run water → milk → wine → honey.

sections.title: Hypocrites grasp nothing, the guided grow; the Hour nears, so seek forgiveness
sections.meaning: Some sit with the Prophet ﷺ, then leave asking, “What did he just say?” Their hearts are sealed because they follow desires, while the guided get more guidance. Are the deniers waiting for the Hour? Its signs have come, and remembering then won’t help. So know there is no god but Allah, and seek forgiveness.
points: They listen, then ask, “What did he just say?” Hearts sealed
The guided are given more guidance and their taqwā
Waiting for the Hour? Its signs have already come
Know: no god but Allah; seek forgiveness for yourself and believers
sections.matters: It sets two kinds of listeners side by side: one leaves with nothing, the other grows. Then it brings everyone back to the core, lā ilāha illā Allāh and seeking forgiveness, before the Hour comes and remembering is too late.
sections.story: The hypocrites reportedly sat through the Prophet’s ﷺ sermons, which criticised them, then left the mosque and mockingly asked Companions such as ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, “What did he just say?”
explained: Some sit listening to the Prophet ﷺ, but nothing reaches them. Leaving, they ask the Companions who have knowledge, “What did he say ānifan, just now?”, uninterested or mocking. Allah sealed their hearts because they followed their desires. Those who seek guidance are given more of it, and Allah grants them their taqwā.

Are they waiting for the Hour to strike suddenly? Its ashrāṭ, signs, have already come, including the sending of the Prophet ﷺ, the last prophet. Once it arrives, remembering is no use. So know lā ilāha illā Allāh and live by it, and seek forgiveness for yourself and all believers. Allah knows your every movement and resting place.
teaches: Listening with the ears but not the heart gains nothing.
Seek guidance and Allah gives you more.
Wake up before the Hour, when reminders no longer help.
Knowledge first, then action: know lā ilāha illā Allāh, then seek forgiveness.
Ask forgiveness for all believers, men and women.
sections.hook: Ayah 16 ends wattabaʿū ahwāʾahum, the same words that close ayah 14. Guidance grows in 17: ihtadaw → zādahum hudā. Ayah 19 gives two commands: fa-ʿlam (know) and wa-staghfir (seek forgiveness).

sections.title: Fighting ordered: the sick-hearted panic, turn back, and face angels at death
sections.meaning: When a surah ordering fighting came, the sick-hearted stared at the Prophet ﷺ like men fainting at death. Turning away would bring corruption, cut family ties and a curse. Do they not reflect on the Quran? Satan lured those who turned back into secret deals with the enemy, and angels will strike them at death.
points: A surah orders fighting; the sick-hearted stare as if dying
Turning away brings corruption and cut family ties; cursed, deaf, blind
Do they not reflect on the Quran, or are hearts locked?
Satan lured the turncoats; they promised the enemy partial obedience
Angels strike their faces and backs; their deeds made worthless
sections.matters: Ayah 20 gives the surah its other name, al-Qitāl. A hard command separates real faith from talk, and the section traces the slide: fear, turning away, secret deals with the enemy, then a harsh death.
sections.story: No single incident. The believers had longed for a surah allowing them to fight; when it came, the hypocrites panicked. Those who “turned back” are either the hypocrites, or People of the Book who rejected the Prophet ﷺ after recognising him.
explained: The believers wished for a surah on fighting. When a clear, binding one came, the sick-hearted stared at the Prophet ﷺ like a man fainting at death. Obedience and good words would have been better. If they turn away, they return to old ways, bloodshed and cutting family ties, and Allah curses them, leaving them deaf and blind to truth.

Do they not reflect on the Quran, or are there locks on their hearts? Those who turned back after guidance was clear were lured by Satan with false hopes. They secretly told the enemies of revelation, “We will obey you in some things,” but Allah knows their secrets. At death the angels will strike their faces and backs.
teaches: Wishing for a hard command is easy; standing firm when it comes is the test.
Turning from Allah’s command leads to corruption and broken family ties.
Reflect on the Quran; a heart that won’t becomes locked.
Secret loyalty to Allah’s enemies is known to Him.
Following what angers Allah wipes out your deeds.
sections.hook: Adbār appears twice: they turned back on their adbār (25), and angels strike their adbār (27). Ayah 28 ends fa-aḥbaṭa aʿmālahum, exactly like ayah 9.

sections.title: Hypocrites exposed, believers tested; don’t weaken, and spend or be replaced
sections.meaning: The hypocrites’ hidden hatred will come out; the Prophet ﷺ will know them by their tone. Allah tests everyone. Believers must obey, not ruin their deeds, and not weaken and call for peace while uppermost. This life is play. Allah doesn’t demand all your wealth, but the stingy harm themselves, and He can replace you.
points: Their hidden hatred will come out; you’ll know them by their tone
Allah tests you to show who strives and stays patient
Deniers can’t harm Allah; obey Him and the Messenger, don’t ruin deeds
Die disbelieving, no forgiveness; don’t weaken and call for peace
This life is play; Allah doesn’t demand all your wealth
The stingy harm themselves; turn away and you’ll be replaced
sections.matters: It closes the surah’s test: hidden hatred comes out, strivers are made known, and deeds are either kept or lost. It ends with what faith costs, courage and spending, and a warning that Allah needs no one.
sections.story: Some Companions thought no sin could harm someone who said lā ilāha illā Allāh; ayah 33 reportedly made them fear for their deeds. When ayah 38 was recited, they asked who would replace them. The Prophet ﷺ put his hand on Salmān al-Fārisī: “This man and his people.”
explained: The hypocrites hid aḍghān, bitter hatred of Islam and its people. Allah could show each of them to the Prophet ﷺ by a mark, but covered them; he will know them by laḥn al-qawl, the slant of their speech. Allah tests everyone to bring the strivers and the patient into the open. Those who oppose the Messenger harm only themselves.

So, believers: obey Allah and the Messenger and don’t spoil your deeds. Whoever dies disbelieving is never forgiven. Don’t weaken and ask for a truce while you are uppermost; Allah is with you. This life is play. He asks only part of your wealth; demand it all and you would resent it. The stingy harm only themselves.
teaches: What is hidden in the heart comes out in speech.
Tests show who truly strives and stays patient.
Deeds can be ruined, so guard them with obedience and sincerity.
Allah is free of need and we are the needy; spending helps the giver.
Allah’s religion doesn’t depend on any one people.
sections.hook: Ayat 32 and 34 open like ayah 1: “those who disbelieved and averted from Allah’s path.” Aḍghān frames the section: yukhrija aḍghānahum (29), yukhrij aḍghānakum (37). The surah ends on page 510.

groups.text: Disbelievers who block Allah’s way lose their deeds. Believers in what came to Muḥammad ﷺ have their sins erased and condition set right.
The reason: disbelievers follow falsehood, and believers follow the truth from their Lord.
In battle, fight until the enemy is overwhelmed, then take captives and free them by favour or ransom. Those killed never lose their deeds.
Allah guides those killed in His cause, sets them right, and admits them to a Paradise He made known to them.
Support Allah and He supports you and steadies your feet. Disbelievers are ruined and lose their deeds, because they hated His revelation.
Earlier deniers were destroyed, and these face the same. Allah protects the believers; the disbelievers have no protector.
Believers enter gardens; disbelievers eat like cattle, bound for the Fire. Towns stronger than Makkah were destroyed with no helper.
Clear proof is not like following desire. Paradise’s rivers of water, milk, wine and honey are not like scalding water.
Hypocrites listen, then ask what he just said; their hearts are sealed. The guided get more guidance and taqwā.
The Hour’s signs have come, and it will strike suddenly. So know there is no god but Allah, and seek forgiveness.
A surah ordering fighting comes, and the sick-hearted stare as if dying. Obedience and being true to Allah would have been better.
Turning away would mean corruption and cut family ties; such people are cursed, deaf and blind. Do they not reflect on the Quran?
Satan lured those who turned back after guidance. They secretly promised the enemies of revelation partial obedience.
At death, angels strike their faces and backs, because they followed what angers Allah. Their deeds are made worthless.
The hypocrites’ hidden hatred will be exposed, known by their tone. Allah tests everyone to show who strives and is patient.
Those who block Allah’s way and oppose the Messenger can’t harm Him. Believers: obey Allah and the Messenger, and don’t ruin your deeds.
Whoever dies a disbeliever is never forgiven. Don’t weaken and call for peace while uppermost; Allah is with you.
This life is play. Allah asks for faith and taqwā, not all your wealth; if He demanded it, you would hold back.
Some of you are stingy, but that harms only themselves. Allah is free of need, you are needy; turn away and He replaces you.

1.explain: Kafarū wa ṣaddū: they disbelieved and blocked others from Islam. Aḍalla aʿmālahum: Allah makes their deeds go to waste, both their plots against the Prophet ﷺ and good deeds like feeding guests, which need faith to count.
1.why: Reportedly about Makkah’s leaders, or specifically the twelve men who fed the Quraysh army at Badr. Others say it is general.

2.explain: Believing in what was sent to Muḥammad ﷺ is named on its own: after his coming, faith means following him. Allah wipes out their sins and sets right their bāl: their condition, or their hearts, in both worlds.
2.why: The believers here are reportedly the Anṣār, or some people of Quraysh; others say it is general.

3.explain: The cause of both outcomes: disbelievers follow al-bāṭil, falsehood, and believers follow al-ḥaqq, the truth from their Lord. This is how Allah shows people the two types and where each one ends up.

4.explain: Strike the necks: fight fully until you have overwhelmed them, then bind captives securely. Afterwards free them as a favour or for ransom, until the war ends. Allah could win without fighting, but tests people through each other.
4.why: Reportedly revealed after Badr, where taking ransom had been criticised (8:67); this ayah allowed release by favour or ransom. Its ending, on those killed, reportedly came at Uḥud, when many Muslims were killed and wounded.

5.explain: Allah guides those killed in His cause, to Paradise and to what benefits them, and sets their state right. Their reward is complete, with nothing to spoil it.

6.explain: ʿArrafahā lahum: He made Paradise known to them. He described it so they longed for it, and there each finds his home more easily than his home in this world. Or: He made it fragrant for them.

7.explain: If you support Allah, by standing up for His religion, calling to it and striving, He supports you against your enemy and makes your feet firm, with steady hearts in battle.

8.explain: Fa-taʿsan lahum: ruin and failure for the disbelievers, the opposite of firm feet. Their deeds are made void, including their plots against the truth, which turn back on them.

9.explain: The reason: they hated what Allah revealed, the Quran and its duties. So He made their deeds worthless (aḥbaṭa).

10.explain: Have they not travelled and seen how earlier deniers ended? Allah destroyed them, their families and their wealth. The disbelievers of Makkah face the like if they don’t believe.

11.explain: Mawlā: protector and helper. Allah protects and helps the believers; the disbelievers have no one to guide them or save them from His punishment.
11.why: Reportedly revealed at Uḥud. When the enemy shouted, “We have al-ʿUzzā and you have no ʿUzzā,” the Prophet ﷺ told the Muslims to answer: “Allah is our protector, and you have no protector.”

12.explain: Believers enter gardens with flowing rivers. Disbelievers enjoy this world and eat like cattle, caring only for their appetites, with no thought of the Hereafter. The Fire will be their mathwā, their lasting home.

13.explain: Many towns stronger than Makkah, in wealth, people and buildings, were destroyed with no helper. Makkah, which drove the Prophet ﷺ out, deserves the same; Allah’s mercy through him holds it back.
13.why: Reportedly revealed as the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah for the Hijrah. Looking back from the cave, he said: “You are the dearest land to Allah and to me. Had its people not driven me out, I would never have left.”

14.explain: Can someone on bayyinah, clear proof and certainty from his Lord, be like someone whose evil deeds are made to look good and who follows desires? The two are not equal.

15.explain: Paradise has rivers of water that never goes stale, milk whose taste never turns, wine that is pure delight without harm, and filtered honey, plus every fruit and forgiveness. Is that like drinking boiling water that tears the bowels?

16.explain: Some sit listening to the Prophet ﷺ without taking anything in. Leaving, they ask knowledgeable Companions, “What did he say ānifan, just now?” Allah sealed their hearts because they followed their desires.
16.why: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ gave sermons criticising the hypocrites. Leaving the mosque, they would mockingly ask Companions such as ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, “What did he just say?”

17.explain: Those who seek guidance get more of it, and Allah grants them their taqwā: He helps them do good and protects them from evil. Two rewards: useful knowledge and righteous action.
17.why: One report says it is about People of the Book who believed.

18.explain: Are they waiting for the Hour to take them baghtatan, suddenly? Its ashrāṭ, signs, have already come, including the sending of the Prophet ﷺ, the last prophet. Once it comes, remembering is useless.

19.explain: Know, and hold firm to, lā ilāha illā Allāh. Seek forgiveness, so the ummah follows your example, and for believing men and women. Allah knows your moving about by day and your resting place by night.

20.explain: The believers wished for a surah on fighting. When a muḥkamah surah came, clear and binding, the hypocrites stared at the Prophet ﷺ like someone fainting at death. Awlā lahum: ruin is near them, or obedience suits them better.

21.explain: Obedience and kind words would have been better. Once fighting was made a firm duty, being true to Allah in faith and obedience would have been best for them.

22.explain: If you turn away, from the command or from faith, would you return to the old ways: corruption, bloodshed and cutting family ties? Or it means: if you are given power over people.
22.why: Reports differ. Most apply it to the hypocrites; on the “given power” reading, one report says it is about the clans of Quraysh who would come to rule.

23.explain: Those who do this are the ones Allah has cursed, driven far from His mercy. He made them deaf to the truth and blind to guidance: ears that hear without accepting.

24.explain: Do they not reflect (yatadabbarūn) on the Quran? It would lead them to every good. Or are there locks on their hearts, shut so tight that its meaning can’t get in?

25.explain: They turned back to disbelief after guidance was clear. Satan made it look good (sawwala) and stretched out false hopes. They are either the hypocrites, or People of the Book who knew the Prophet ﷺ yet rejected him.

26.explain: They told the idolaters, who hated revelation, “We will obey you in part”: helping against the Prophet ﷺ and holding back from fighting. They said it secretly, but Allah knows their secrets and exposed them.

27.explain: How will it be when the angels take their souls, beating their faces and their backs? Their souls cling to their bodies, so the angels pull them out harshly.

28.explain: That is because they followed what angers Allah and disliked what pleases Him, faith and obedience. So He made their deeds worthless.

29.explain: Did those with disease in their hearts think Allah would never bring out their aḍghān, the hidden hatred and envy they feel toward Islam and its people? He will, and trials will reveal it.

30.explain: Allah could show each hypocrite to the Prophet ﷺ by a sīmā, a mark, but chose to cover them. Still, he will know them by laḥn al-qawl, the slant of their words. The heart slips out through the tongue.

31.explain: Allah tests you, with commands like fighting, until He makes known who strives and who is patient. He already knows; the test brings it into the open and shows your true state.

32.explain: Those who disbelieve, block Allah’s way and oppose the Messenger after guidance was clear can’t harm Allah at all. Their efforts against Islam fail, and their good deeds bring no reward.
32.why: Reportedly about the men who fed the Quraysh army at Badr, or about the Jewish tribes of Qurayẓah and an-Naḍīr.

33.explain: Obey Allah and the Messenger, and don’t spoil your deeds: by leaving faith, by showing off, by reminding people of favours, or by sins. Jurists differ on whether a voluntary act, once begun, must be finished.
33.why: Some Companions thought no sin could harm anyone who says lā ilāha illā Allāh, just as no deed helps someone who associates partners with Allah. This ayah reportedly came, and they began to fear sins could ruin deeds.

34.explain: Those who disbelieve, block Allah’s way and die as disbelievers will never be forgiven. The door stays open until death: had they repented before it, Allah would forgive them.
34.why: Reportedly about the Quraysh leaders killed at Badr and thrown into the well, though its ruling is general.

35.explain: Don’t weaken and call for a truce while you are al-aʿlawn, uppermost. Allah is with you and won’t cut your reward. The ban is on seeking peace from weakness; a treaty that serves the Muslims, like Ḥudaybiyah, remained allowed.

36.explain: This life is only play and distraction, except what is done for Allah. Believe and have taqwā and He gives your reward. He doesn’t ask for your wealth, or not all of it: He has no need of it.

37.explain: If He demanded all of it and pressed you (yuḥfikum), you would hold back, and your aḍghān, resentment, would come out. So He asks for only a small share.

38.explain: You are called to spend in Allah’s cause, yet some hold back, and that harms only themselves. Allah is al-Ghanī, free of need; you are the needy. Turn away and He brings another people, not like you.
